rule: One large left-right symmetric hollow frame (1-2 colours, possibly split into non-touching mirror halves) is identified by the colours of the largest 8-connected multicolour object. Every cell of those colours is frame. The output is the frame's bounding box, with each background hole filled by translating the scattered monochrome pieces so they tile the holes exactly. The resulting colouring is unique.
scope: Random scenes: symmetric frame masks of 3-8 columns by 4-10 rows. The masks are optionally also top-bottom symmetric, can have disconnected fragments, and have one colour or two split at a row. There are 3-10 pieces of up to 8 cells, coloured per orbit/shape class. Inputs are 10-20 per side by default, or 10-30 when pinned. Background is any colour. Pieces sit outside the frame bbox plus a ring and are separated even diagonally. Frame widths other than 5 and grid sizes other than 13/15 are synthetic extensions, as are output abutment of same-coloured pieces in about half the scenes. Not supported: rotated/reflected pieces, pieces sharing frame colours, pieces inside the bbox, asymmetric frames, frames larger than 8x10. Explicit mode reproduces the fixtures and accepts other symmetric, validated scenes.

known_limitations: Frames are capped at 8x10 and holes at 28 cells, even on large pinned grids.
Piece shapes come from random region growth within mirror domains. They are not sampled from a shape library, so some shapes (e.g. long bars) are less frequent than in the fixtures.

The naive-search cost guard covers a finite set of piece orders. A reference that enumerates objects in another order could in principle search longer, but the output would still be correct, since the colouring is unique.
Explicit mode does not enforce piece-count limits or fragment-size limits; the docstring states this.
Small pinned dimensions (10) give narrow free strips, so they rely on rejection sampling within a 3000-iteration bound.
Bounded solver agreement and control checks do not prove complete coverage of every interpretation of the task.

authored_constraints: Hole colouring by translated pieces is unique. It is checked with a deduplicated exact-cover count, and a budget overrun is rejected.
Equal piece shapes always share a colour; otherwise a swap would make the colouring ambiguous.
Every largest 8-connected frame part is strictly larger than any piece and contains every frame colour, so the reference's largest-multicolour-object step recovers all frame colours.
Piece colours differ from the background and all frame colours. The frame colours differ from the background.
Pieces are 4-connected, in bounds, outside the frame bbox, and not 8-adjacent to frame cells or to each other. Random scenes also keep a 1-cell ring around the bbox clear.
The background is strictly the most frequent input colour.
The frame mask touches all four sides of its bounding box and is left-right symmetric.

A naive index-based first-hole backtracking search stays within a node budget. This is checked for several piece orders, including input scan order and random permutations; explicit scenes check scan order and its reverse.
At most 4 copies of any (colour, shape) and 3-10 pieces in random scenes; all generation loops are bounded.
